title: chore: initialize aidevops framework scaffolding
body:
## Summary

Initialize the aidevops framework for task tracking, planning, and AI-assisted development workflows in this repo.

## Context

PR #7 was closed due to merge conflicts with the base branch. The scaffolding work needs to be re-attempted on a fresh branch.

## Implementation

1. Add `.aidevops.json` config with planning, git-workflow, code-quality, time-tracking, and security features enabled (database/beads disabled — not needed for a WP plugin)
2. Add `TODO.md` with TOON-enhanced task tracking
3. Add `todo/PLANS.md` and `todo/tasks/` directory
4. Add `AGENTS.md` with build, lint, test, and code style guidelines

Reference PR #7 for the original implementation (branch `chore/aidevops-init` still exists — use `gh pr diff 7` for context, but create a fresh branch to avoid conflicts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.aidevops.json` present and valid
- [ ] `TODO.md` present with correct TOON format
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` present with project-specific guidelines
- [ ] CI passes

title: fix(ci): Cypress E2E fails — plugin slug mismatch after rename
body:
## Summary

Cypress E2E tests fail on every run (including main) with:

```
AssertionError: Timed out retrying after 10000ms: Expected to find element: `[data-slug="ai-provider-for-any-compatible-endpoint"]`, but never found it.
```

## Root Cause

The plugin was renamed (see PR #1 — `refactor/rename-plugin-to-ultimate-ai-connector`). The Cypress test in `tests/e2e/plugin-activation.cy.js` still uses the old plugin slug `ai-provider-for-any-compatible-endpoint` but the actual plugin slug after rename is likely different.

## Evidence

- Run #23872154302 (chore/aidevops-init branch): FAILURE
- Run #23868466433 (main): FAILURE  
- Run #23868204773 (main): FAILURE
- Run #23867111083 (main): FAILURE

This is systemic — fails on every branch including main.

## Fix

Update `tests/e2e/plugin-activation.cy.js` to use the correct plugin slug that matches the renamed plugin's directory name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cypress test uses correct plugin slug matching the renamed plugin
- [ ] Cypress E2E passes on main
- [ ] CI green

title: chore: upgrade GitHub Actions from Node.js 20 to Node.js 24
body:
## Problem

GitHub Actions is deprecating Node.js 20. Actions running on Node.js 20 will be forced to Node.js 24 starting **June 2, 2026**, and Node.js 20 will be removed from runners on **September 16, 2026**.

This repo's workflows use actions that still run on Node.js 20, producing deprecation warnings on every run.

## Required upgrades

| Current | Upgrade to |
|---------|------------|
| `actions/cache@v4` | `actions/cache@v5` |
| `actions/checkout@v4` | `actions/checkout@v6` |
| `actions/setup-node@v4` | `actions/setup-node@v6` |
| `actions/upload-artifact@v4` | `actions/upload-artifact@v7` |
| `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` | Keep `@v2` -- set `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true` env var until upstream ships Node 24 support |

`shivammathur/setup-php@v2` is already on Node 24 (v2.37.0) -- no change needed.

## How

EDIT: `.github/workflows/*.yml` -- find-and-replace the action version tags per the table above.

For `softprops/action-gh-release`, add this env var to the workflow or job level until upstream releases a Node 24 version:

```yaml
env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true
```

## Verification

After merging, trigger a workflow run and confirm no Node.js 20 deprecation warnings appear in the annotations.

## References

- [GitHub blog: Deprecation of Node 20 on GitHub Actions runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/)

title: Provider availability check makes blocking HTTP request on every page load
body:
## Problem

When the plugin registers a provider with the WordPress AI Client SDK at `init:5`, the SDK's `ListModelsApiBasedProviderAvailability::isConfigured()` method makes a **blocking HTTP request** to the endpoint's `/models` URL on every page load where the availability is checked. This adds 7+ seconds to admin page loads and can cause OOM crashes on memory-constrained environments (FrankenPHP, limited php-fpm pools).

### Observed impact

- **wp-admin page load time**: 1.4s without plugin → 8.5s with plugin (7.1s regression)
- **Memory**: the extended HTTP request + response parsing pushes FrankenPHP past the 512MB PHP `memory_limit` on multisite installations, causing HTTP 500 errors
- **Environment**: WordPress 7.0-RC2 multisite (57 sites), FrankenPHP v1.4.4, PHP 8.4

### Root cause chain

1. **`createProviderAvailability()` in `class-provider.php:83-86`** returns a `ListModelsApiBasedProviderAvailability` instance, which checks availability by calling `listModelMetadata()` — a live HTTP request to the endpoint.

2. **The SDK's model metadata cache is ineffective.** `AbstractApiBasedModelMetadataDirectory::getModelMetadataMap()` (SDK `line 77`) caches via `$this->cached()` with a 86400s TTL, but the cache backend is `WP_AI_Client_Cache` which uses `wp_cache_set/get` (WordPress object cache). Without a persistent object cache (Redis, Memcached, Docket Cache), the cache is in-memory only and **cold on every request**. FrankenPHP's threaded mode and standard php-fpm both start with empty object caches per request.

3. **`increase_timeout` filter in `http-filters.php:26-41`** sets the timeout to 360 seconds for any HTTP request matching the endpoint host. If the endpoint is slow or unreachable, a single page load blocks for up to 6 minutes.

4. **The availability check can be triggered from multiple paths:**
   - `connectors.php:625` — `isProviderConfigured()` for every connector on the Connectors settings page
   - `ProviderRegistry.php:231` — `findModelsMetadataForSupport()` when any AI feature searches for capable models
   - Any code calling `AiClient::isConfigured()` for this provider

### Why this only manifests on some sites

- Sites with a persistent object cache (Redis, Docket Cache) see the 24h cache TTL work correctly — the HTTP request only fires once per day
- Sites without persistent object cache (common in development, some production setups) fire the HTTP request on **every page load**
- The `http_request_args` filter also runs on every `wp_remote_*` call, adding a `get_option()` call per HTTP request (minor but cumulative)

## Proposed fixes

### 1. Use a WordPress transient instead of object cache for model list (primary fix)

The SDK's `WithDataCachingTrait` delegates to the PSR-16 cache adapter, which maps to `wp_cache_*`. Replace or supplement this with `set_transient()` / `get_transient()` which persists to the database and survives across requests regardless of object cache backend.

Implementation: override `getModelMetadataMap()` in `CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory` to use `get_transient('ultimate_ai_connector_models_' . md5($endpoint_url))` with a 24h expiry, falling back to `sendListModelsRequest()` on cache miss.

### 2. Implement a non-blocking availability check (secondary fix)

Override `createProviderAvailability()` in `CompatibleEndpointProvider` to return a simple configuration-based check instead of `ListModelsApiBasedProviderAvailability`:

```php
protected static function createProviderAvailability(): ProviderAvailabilityInterface {
    // Check if the endpoint is configured, not if it's reachable.
    // Reachability is verified lazily when the user actually uses the provider.
    return new class implements ProviderAvailabilityInterface {
        public function isConfigured(): bool {
            return ! empty( CompatibleEndpointProvider::$endpointUrl );
        }
    };
}
```

This avoids the blocking HTTP request entirely. The actual endpoint validation happens when the user first makes an AI request, not on every page load.

### 3. Cap the `increase_timeout` filter to AI generation requests only

The 360s timeout is only needed for actual AI generation requests (`/chat/completions`). Availability checks (`/models`) should use a short timeout (5-10s), and the filter should not apply to unrelated HTTP requests:

```php
function increase_timeout( array $parsed_args, string $url ): array {
    // Only extend timeout for chat completions, not model listing
    if ( str_contains( $url, '/chat/completions' ) ) {
        $timeout = (int) get_option( 'ultimate_ai_connector_timeout', 360 );
        $parsed_args['timeout'] = max( (float) ( $parsed_args['timeout'] ?? 30 ), (float) $timeout );
    }
    return $parsed_args;
}
```

## Reproduction steps

1. Install WordPress 7.0+ multisite with no persistent object cache
2. Activate this plugin and configure an endpoint URL (e.g. `https://api.synthetic.new/openai/v1`)
3. Load any wp-admin page and measure load time
4. Deactivate the plugin and compare — expect ~7s improvement

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `inc/class-provider.php:83-86` — override `createProviderAvailability()` to use config-based check
- EDIT: `inc/class-model-directory.php` — add transient-based caching layer around `sendListModelsRequest()`
- EDIT: `inc/http-filters.php:26-41` — scope the timeout extension to `/chat/completions` requests only
- EDIT: `inc/class-provider-factory.php:107-111` — same availability fix for `DynamicCompatibleEndpointProvider`

title: Supervisor health dashboard stale: 2d2h (#118)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard at #118 last refreshed `2026-04-24T19:04:08Z` — **2d2h ago** (threshold: 2d0h). The `stats-wrapper.sh` scheduler is likely failing silently.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status (macOS):

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Ultimate-Multisite/ai-provider-for-any-compatible-endpoint/issues/118 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **Missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 118 --repo Ultimate-Multisite/ai-provider-for-any-compatible-endpoint` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: fix: CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory namespace resolution fails in MultiProviderRoutingTest on WP 7.0-nightly
body:
## Problem

`tests/php/MultiProviderRoutingTest::test_directory_cache_key_includes_endpoint_url` errors on WP 7.0-nightly:

```
Error: Class "UltimateAiConnectorCompatibleEndpoints\Tests\CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory" not found
tests/php/MultiProviderRoutingTest.php:339
```

**Root cause**: Lines 339 and 343 use `new CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory()` without a fully-qualified name or `use` statement. Inside the `UltimateAiConnectorCompatibleEndpoints\Tests\` namespace, PHP resolves this as `UltimateAiConnectorCompatibleEndpoints\Tests\CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory` — which does not exist. The class lives in `UltimateAiConnectorCompatibleEndpoints\CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory`.

**Why it passes on WP 6.9**: Lines 321–323 call `markTestSkipped()` when the AI Client SDK is absent. On WP 6.9, `AbstractOpenAiCompatibleModelMetadataDirectory` is not available so the test is **skipped** and the namespace bug is never hit. On WP 7.0-nightly the SDK is bundled and the test runs, exposing the bug.

Lines 325–326 already do this correctly using a fully-qualified string variable:

```php
$directory_class = 'UltimateAiConnectorCompatibleEndpoints\\CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory';
$alpha           = new $directory_class( '...' );
```

Lines 339 and 343 should reuse `$directory_class` instead of the bare class name.

## Fix

**File**: `tests/php/MultiProviderRoutingTest.php`

Change lines 339 and 343 from:

```php
$alpha_dup   = new CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory( 'http://alpha.example.test/v1' );
$alpha_slash = new CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory( 'http://alpha.example.test/v1/' );
```

To:

```php
$alpha_dup   = new $directory_class( 'http://alpha.example.test/v1' );
$alpha_slash = new $directory_class( 'http://alpha.example.test/v1/' );
```

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/php/MultiProviderRoutingTest.php` must pass on both WP 6.9 and WP 7.0-nightly.
- CI workflow **Tests → PHPUnit (WP 7.0-nightly)** must show green (28 tests, 0 errors).

## Evidence

- Failed CI run: https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-compatible-endpoints/actions/runs/25946434756/job/76275393136
- Surfaced by post-merge CI on PR #130
- WP 6.9 PHPUnit ✅ (test skipped due to absent SDK) | WP 7.0-nightly PHPUnit ❌ (SDK present, test runs)

title: Thinking-aware OpenAI-compatible endpoints (DeepSeek, Ollama, LM Studio) silently drop reasoning round-trip
body:
## Summary

`CompatibleEndpointModel` extends `WordPress\AiClient\Providers\OpenAiCompatibleImplementation\AbstractOpenAiCompatibleTextGenerationModel` and inherits its **unconditional stripping of thought-channel `MessagePart`s on outbound** ([`AbstractOpenAiCompatibleTextGenerationModel.php` L235-237 upstream](https://github.com/WordPress/php-ai-client/blob/main/src/Providers/OpenAiCompatibleImplementation/AbstractOpenAiCompatibleTextGenerationModel.php#L235-L237)):

```php
if ($part->getChannel()->isThought()) {
    // The OpenAI Chat Completions API spec does not support annotating thought parts as input,
    // so we instead skip them.
    return null;
}
```

That stripping is correct for plain OpenAI Chat Completions, but **this plugin doesn't know which endpoint the user has configured**. When users point it at a thinking-aware OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama with a reasoning model, LM Studio with a thinking model, a DeepSeek-flavoured proxy, etc.) we silently drop the thinking content the endpoint expects to see round-tripped.

For DeepSeek-flavoured endpoints specifically this produces a hard `400` from the server:

> The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.

For Ollama / LM Studio thinking models the failure mode is softer — degraded quality on subsequent turns instead of a hard error — but the underlying gap is the same.

## Reproduction

1. Point this plugin at a DeepSeek-style endpoint, or at an Ollama install with a thinking-capable model.
2. Run any tool-using multi-turn prompt where the assistant first calls a tool, then is asked a follow-up question that requires another tool call.
3. Either observe `400` on the second request (DeepSeek) or degraded quality (Ollama).

The same bug class was reported and fixed for the dedicated `ai-provider-for-deepseek` plugin in a recent PR (the fix overrides `prepareGenerateTextParams` to re-attach `reasoning_content` on assistant entries). That fix is provider-specific and doesn't cover anyone using this generic plugin against a DeepSeek-flavoured endpoint.

## Why it matters here specifically

Of all the `ai-provider-for-*` plugins, this one has the **widest blast radius** because the endpoint is user-configurable. The other plugins either:

- override `prepareGenerateTextParams` for their specific provider's wire shape (Anthropic, OpenAI Responses API), or
- patch the gap explicitly (DeepSeek, via per-turn `reasoning_content` re-attachment).

This plugin inherits the SDK base verbatim (68 LoC, only overrides `createRequest` for URL routing) — so whatever quirks the user's endpoint has are not represented at the wire layer.

## Background

This is part of a class of issues stemming from `php-ai-client`'s `AbstractOpenAiCompatibleTextGenerationModel` treating "OpenAI-compatible" as a single fixed wire spec when in practice it's a spectrum that includes thinking extensions (DeepSeek's `reasoning_content`, Ollama's `/api/chat` thinking output, etc.). Tracking links:

- `php-ai-client` PR #154 — introduced the unconditional thought stripping (labelled bug, merged Dec 2025).
- `php-ai-client` PR #216 — added `MessagePart` thought-signature and `TokenUsage` thought-token DTO surface (merged Mar 2026), with the author explicitly noting "once this is launched, we should update the provider implementations to support both where applicable".
- `WordPress/ai-provider-for-openai` #13 — companion issue for adopting #216 in the OpenAI plugin (placeholder, open).

## Proposed fix

Two viable approaches:

**A. Endpoint-aware (preferred, no upstream dependency).** Add an "endpoint quirks" setting in the connector card: a small dropdown like `Endpoint type: [Generic / DeepSeek-compatible (thinking-mode) / Ollama-thinking / …]`. When set to a thinking-aware option, override `prepareGenerateTextParams` in `CompatibleEndpointModel` to emit `reasoning_content` (DeepSeek) or `thinking` (Ollama) on assistant entries that issued tool calls, mirroring the pattern in [`ai-provider-for-deepseek`'s recent patch](https://github.com/sajjadh47/ai-provider-for-deepseek/pull/1).

Default stays at `Generic` so plain OpenAI Chat Completions clones (the original intent) keep working identically.

**B. Wait for upstream.** Once `php-ai-client` exposes a hook on `AbstractOpenAiCompatibleTextGenerationModel` for subclasses to opt into thought-part transmission (no upstream issue yet — should probably file one), bump the SDK version constraint and adopt it. Lower maintenance burden but couples release timing to the upstream.

A is recommended because it's a small, self-contained change with an explicit user opt-in, and because users hitting this hard 400 today need a fix that doesn't depend on upstream cadence.

## Files of interest

- `inc/class-model.php` — the 68-line `CompatibleEndpointModel` that needs a `prepareGenerateTextParams` override on the thinking-aware code path.
- `inc/settings.php` — add the endpoint-type setting.
- `src/provider-presets.js` — surface the setting in the React connector card.
- `inc/class-provider-factory.php` — pass the endpoint-type setting into the model on construction.

## Verification

After fix, repeat the reproduction against a DeepSeek-flavoured endpoint with `reasoning.effort=high` + a multi-step tool-using prompt; expect zero 400s and `reasoning_content` to appear on every assistant entry in the subsequent request body.

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`In PHP, what does the second argument of `class_exists()` and `interface_exists()` do, and does passing `false` disable autoloading?`

💡 Result:

In PHP, the second argument of class_exists and interface_exists is the $autoload flag. 1) What the second argument does - class_exists(string $class, bool $autoload = true): the $autoload parameter controls whether PHP will attempt to autoload the class (via spl_autoload) if it hasn’t been loaded yet. [1] - interface_exists(string $interface, bool $autoload = true): the $autoload parameter controls whether PHP will attempt to autoload the interface (via spl_autoload) if it hasn’t been loaded yet. [2] 2) Does passing false disable autoloading? - Yes. If you pass false as the second argument, class_exists / interface_exists will not call spl_autoload to try to load the class/interface. [1][2] Example: - class_exists('SomeClass', false) returns true only if SomeClass is already defined; it will not trigger autoloading to make it appear. [1] - interface_exists('SomeInterface', false) behaves the same way for interfaces. [2]

Citations:

- 1: https://www.php.net/function.class-exists
- 2: https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.interface-exists.php

title: Migrate build, E2E, and release tooling to pnpm
body:
## Goal

Migrate build, PHPUnit/E2E tooling, documentation, CI, and release packaging from npm to pnpm.

## Why this repository benefits

- The npm lockfile exceeds 27,000 lines and covers `@wordpress/scripts`, `@wordpress/env`, and Cypress.
- Node installs are duplicated across release and E2E jobs.
- npm/npx assumptions are spread across workflows, documentation, test helpers, and PHP setup messages.
- pnpm provides meaningful cache/storage savings and stricter dependency correctness for this build graph.

## Implementation scope

- Update `package.json`; replace `package-lock.json` with `pnpm-lock.yaml` and pin pnpm plus the supported Node range.
- Migrate `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` to explicit pnpm setup, cache, and frozen installs.
- Replace locked local tool execution with `pnpm exec`; do not use `pnpm dlx` for Cypress/wp-env already represented by devDependencies.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `docs/testing.md`, and `bin/run-wp-phpunit.php` messages.
- Keep `.distignore` and `composer.json` archive exclusions synchronized for `pnpm-lock.yaml`/workspace metadata.
- Audit `webpack.config.js` for root-resolved Babel packages and declare direct dependencies.
- Make the build-to-archive sequence explicit rather than relying on implicit npm lifecycle chaining; remove or verify `$npm_package_name` assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- All Node workflows use the pinned pnpm version and frozen lockfile installs.
- E2E tools execute from the lockfile without runtime downloads.
- The expected plugin ZIP is produced with the same root and runtime contents.
- Distribution archives exclude Node source, stores, lock/workspace metadata, and dev dependencies.
- Current developer guidance and diagnostic output use pnpm.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
pnpm run test:php
pnpm run wp-env:start
pnpm run test:e2e
pnpm run wp-env:stop
composer validate --strict
unzip -l ultimate-ai-connector-compatible-endpoints.zip
git grep -nE '\b(npm ci|npm run|npx)\b' -- package.json .github AGENTS.md docs bin
```

title: t4: Fix cloud model selection and structured output compatibility
body:
## Problem

OpenAI-compatible cloud providers such as Mammouth.ai expose three connector integration gaps:

- the Connectors UI queries `/models` without resolving the saved provider API key;
- a configured default model can lose to the WordPress AI plugin's built-in text-model preferences;
- structured-output requests inherit a `response_format.json_schema` shape that strict OpenAI-compatible gateways reject because the nested `schema` member is absent.

The Mammouth support report shows LiteLLM raising `KeyError: schema` for taxonomy and editorial-note features while plain-text features succeed.

## Files

EDIT: `src/index.jsx`
EDIT: `inc/rest-api.php`
EDIT: `inc/provider-registration.php`
EDIT: `inc/class-model.php`
EDIT: `build/connector.js`

## Reference pattern

Use the saved provider ID to resolve endpoint credentials server-side. Do not place API keys in URLs. Preserve generic OpenAI-compatible behavior and keep image generation out of this change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Saved cloud providers can populate their model selector using their configured API key.
- [ ] Configured connector defaults are prepended to `wpai_preferred_text_models` in provider order.
- [ ] JSON-schema output uses a named OpenAI-compatible envelope containing `json_schema.schema`.
- [ ] Plain JSON-object output remains unchanged when no schema is provided.
- [ ] The production JavaScript bundle is rebuilt.
- [ ] Existing PHP tests and the production build pass.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run build
pnpm run test:php
php -l inc/class-model.php
php -l inc/rest-api.php
php -l inc/provider-registration.php
```

## Scope

Provider-agnostic image-generation support is intentionally separate because Mammouth returns images through Chat Completions while the SDK's generic image model uses the Images API.

title: t5: Add provider-compatible image generation
body:
## Problem

The connector currently advertises every discovered model as text generation only and `DynamicCompatibleEndpointProvider::createModel()` can instantiate only `CompatibleEndpointModel`. This prevents compatible endpoints from exposing image-generation models through the WordPress AI Client.

Providers do not share one image wire protocol:

- Standard OpenAI-compatible providers use `POST /images/generations` and return `data[].url` or `data[].b64_json`.
- Mammouth.ai-compatible gateways can generate images through `POST /chat/completions` and return image payloads under `choices[].message.images`.

Adding the SDK's generic image capability without protocol selection would route some providers to the wrong endpoint and response parser.

## Goal

Add provider-agnostic image generation with explicit, extensible protocol selection and normalized WordPress AI Client results. Preserve existing text-only behavior unless image support is configured or reliably discovered.

## Files

EDIT: `inc/settings.php`
EDIT: `inc/class-model-directory.php`
EDIT: `inc/class-provider.php`
EDIT: `inc/class-provider-factory.php`
ADD: `inc/class-image-model.php` or protocol-specific image model classes following the existing text-model pattern
EDIT: `src/index.jsx`
EDIT: `build/connector.js`
EDIT/ADD: focused files under `tests/php/`

If implementation reveals a better class split, keep protocol request/response handling isolated behind a small adapter boundary rather than branching throughout provider registration.

## Reference patterns

- Follow `CompatibleEndpointModel` for endpoint URL registration, request construction, authentication, timeout options, and provider metadata.
- Follow the installed SDK's `AbstractOpenAiCompatibleImageGenerationModel` for `images/generations` request options and conversion into `GenerativeAiResult` candidates.
- Follow `CompatibleEndpointModelDirectory` for rebuilding fresh `ModelMetadata` DTOs and avoiding persistent serialization of SDK enum objects.
- Keep the UI's saved API key server-side; never add credentials to URLs, issue output, logs, or browser-readable model-discovery parameters.

## Requirements

1. Add a per-provider image protocol setting with a safe default such as disabled/none. Initial supported values should cover the standard Images API and Chat Completions image responses; design the setting so additional protocols can be added without provider-name checks.
2. Add an explicit image-model selection or capability override. Do not classify arbitrary `/models` entries as image-capable from brittle model-name heuristics alone.
3. Emit `CapabilityEnum::imageGeneration()` only for models configured as image-capable, while retaining text capabilities for normal models.
4. Update legacy and dynamic provider factories so image-capable metadata creates the appropriate image model and text metadata continues creating `CompatibleEndpointModel`.
5. Support standard `images/generations` responses containing remote URLs or base64 image data.
6. Support Chat Completions image responses under `choices[].message.images`, including direct URLs and data URLs/base64 representations that the gateway returns.
7. Normalize both protocols into the SDK's `GenerativeAiResult`, `Candidate`, `Message`, `MessagePart`, and `File` DTOs with a valid image MIME type.
8. Preserve authentication, configured endpoint isolation, timeout behavior, custom options where compatible, and actionable error messages for malformed or unsupported responses.
9. Keep existing providers text-only by default so this feature cannot route ordinary chat models through image endpoints.
10. Rebuild the committed production JavaScript bundle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A provider configured for the standard Images API can generate an image from `data[].url` and `data[].b64_json` responses.
- [ ] A provider configured for Chat Completions image generation can parse `choices[].message.images` into the same SDK result shape.
- [ ] The configured image model is discoverable with `imageGeneration` capability and instantiates an image-generation model.
- [ ] Text-only models and providers retain their current capabilities and request path.
- [ ] Unknown/disabled protocols do not advertise image generation.
- [ ] A malformed response returns an SDK-compatible exception that identifies the missing/invalid response field without exposing credentials.
- [ ] Multi-provider configurations can use different image protocols independently.
- [ ] Settings sanitization rejects unsupported protocol values and preserves backward compatibility for saved provider arrays.
- [ ] Focused positive and negative PHP tests cover capability mapping, factory routing, both protocol parsers, malformed responses, and text-path regression.
- [ ] `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test:php`, and PHP syntax checks pass.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run build
pnpm run test:php
php -l inc/class-image-model.php
php -l inc/class-model-directory.php
php -l inc/class-provider-factory.php
php -l inc/settings.php
```

Where the local WordPress version lacks the AI Client SDK, also run the SDK-dependent tests against a WordPress version that includes the installed image-generation abstractions.

## Scope and hazards

- Do not hard-code Mammouth.ai or any other vendor into the core protocol selection.
- Do not silently fall back from one protocol to another after an authenticated request fails; that can duplicate billed image requests. Automatic selection is acceptable only when based on configuration or non-generating capability metadata.
- Do not fetch returned remote image URLs server-side unless the SDK contract requires it; preserve the SDK's `File` representation and existing HTTP safety rules.
- Image editing, variations, video generation, and provider-specific moderation controls are out of scope unless required for the minimum adapter boundary.

## Evidence

- `inc/class-model-directory.php` currently assigns only text-generation and chat-history capabilities to every model.
- `inc/class-provider-factory.php` currently accepts only text-generation capability and throws for other model capabilities.
- The installed SDK's `AbstractOpenAiCompatibleImageGenerationModel` hard-codes `images/generations` and parses `data[].url` / `data[].b64_json`, so Chat Completions image providers require a separate adapter.
- The Mammouth compatibility investigation tracked in #148 observed image payloads under `choices[].message.images`; PR #149 intentionally keeps image work outside the text-path fix.

title: t6: Add Mammouth preset and clarify endpoint type
body:
## Problem

A customer testing the Mammouth.ai compatibility fixes confirmed that authenticated model discovery, manual model selection, and structured-output features work. The remaining setup experience has several problems:

- Mammouth.ai is absent from the provider preset list.
- Endpoint type does not make the normal Mammouth.ai choice obvious or clearly distinguish thinking-history formatting from provider/model selection.
- Model loading has no visible loading, empty, or error state; failures are silently discarded.
- A new authenticated provider cannot use server-side `config_id` credential resolution until it is saved, but the UI attempts discovery before that and does not clearly reload after Save.
- General field edits can trigger model requests, while endpoint/API-key changes can retain stale cached results.

The customer originally reported that the root URL worked while `/v1` did not:
https://wordpress.org/support/topic/working-with-mammouth-ai/#post-19011661

Authenticated verification on 2026-09-09 could not reproduce that path split: root and `/v1` model and Chat Completions resources all returned HTTP 200.

## Goal

Make Mammouth.ai easy to configure without vendor-specific request routing. Add its canonical preset, explain Endpoint type in user terms, and make authenticated model loading deliberate, observable, retryable, and cache-correct.

## Files

EDIT: `src/provider-presets.js`
EDIT: `src/index.jsx`
EDIT: `build/connector.js`
EDIT/ADD: focused tests under `tests/e2e/` when practical with the existing Cypress setup

PHP path customization is not currently justified. If implementation finds a genuine server-side defect, document the evidence before expanding the file scope.

## Reference patterns

- Follow existing cloud entries in `src/provider-presets.js`; keep alphabetical ordering.
- Keep saved `endpoint_type` values `generic`, `deepseek`, and `ollama` backward compatible.
- Continue using the server-side `config_id` credential-resolution path in `inc/rest-api.php`; never place credentials in URLs or browser-readable query parameters.
- Keep image-generation work in #150.

## Requirements

1. Add a cloud preset named `Mammouth.ai` with canonical base URL `https://api.mammouth.ai/v1` and keep Endpoint type `generic`.
2. Do not add Mammouth-specific PHP routing or separate discovery/generation URL fields. The connector already appends `models` and `chat/completions`, and live tests confirm the canonical base works for both.
3. Clarify URL help: the field takes an API base URL, not a complete operation URL.
4. Clarify Endpoint type:
   - Generic is recommended for Mammouth.ai and most OpenAI-compatible APIs.
   - DeepSeek-compatible reattaches prior reasoning through `reasoning_content`.
   - Ollama reattaches prior thought content through `thinking`.
   - The setting does not select a provider or model and normally does not change plain responses.
5. Replace silent model loading with explicit per-provider states: initial guidance, loading, success/model count, empty response, actionable error, and retry.
6. For a new authenticated provider, clearly require Save before server-side model discovery, or provide an equally secure flow that does not expose the key in a query string. After successful Save, invalidate as needed and fetch models using the saved `config_id` without requiring a page reload.
7. Do not fetch models on Name, API key, timeout, enabled, endpoint-type, or partial URL edits. Use an explicit load/test action or a narrowly scoped/debounced valid endpoint transition.
8. Invalidate the relevant cache after endpoint or credential changes and prevent concurrent duplicate requests for the same provider/endpoint.
9. Preserve Cancel behavior so unsaved additions and edits are discarded.
10. Rebuild the committed production JavaScript bundle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Searching presets for `Mammouth`, `mammouth`, or `Mammouth.ai` returns `Mammouth.ai` and fills `https://api.mammouth.ai/v1` plus the name when empty.
- [ ] Selecting the preset leaves Endpoint type set to Generic.
- [ ] Endpoint URL help explains base-URL semantics and Endpoint type help visibly recommends Generic for normal Mammouth.ai use.
- [ ] A new blank provider explains how to load models rather than showing an unexplained Auto-select-only state.
- [ ] After Save, an authenticated provider loads models through `config_id` with visible progress and no page reload.
- [ ] Empty and failed discovery responses remain visible and offer a retry instead of being silently ignored.
- [ ] Unrelated field edits do not produce model requests; duplicate in-flight requests are suppressed.
- [ ] Endpoint or credential changes cannot reuse stale model results.
- [ ] Existing provider presets and saved endpoint-type values remain unchanged.
- [ ] Cancel discards temporary providers and edits.
- [ ] `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test:php`, and `git diff --check` pass; targeted Cypress coverage passes when added.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run build
pnpm run test:php
```

Inspect `build/connector.js`. In the local WordPress admin, verify preset search, Save-then-load behavior, loading/error/retry states, cache invalidation, and Cancel. When using a live credential, inject it through an approved secret channel and never log it.

## Hazards

- Never publish or place the customer credential in an issue, command output, fixture, URL, or model-discovery query.
- Do not silently retry billed generation requests against another path.
- Do not infer Endpoint type from the selected model name; Mammouth.ai routes multiple upstream providers.
- Do not encode the historical `/v1` report as current API behavior unless it becomes reproducible.

## Evidence

- Current authenticated model discovery returned 98 byte-identical model records from both `/models` and `/v1/models`.
- Minimal plain text requests succeeded at both `/chat/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`.
- The connector's named JSON Schema envelope succeeded at `/v1/chat/completions`.
- A WordPress 7.1 / AI Client 1.3.1 integration probe with the current plugin and `https://api.mammouth.ai/v1` securely resolved the saved key through `config_id`, returned all 98 models, selected `gpt-4.1-nano`, and generated `{"status":"ok"}`. Temporary settings were restored.
- `src/provider-presets.js` has no Mammouth entry.
- `src/index.jsx` always passes `isLoadingModels={ false }`, silently catches discovery failures, fetches during general provider updates, and does not explicitly refetch after Save.
- A browser audit reproduced the missing preset and absent loading/empty/error feedback; Cancel correctly discarded the temporary provider.

title: chore: stop tracking local .aidevops.json
body:
<!-- aidevops:project-config-migration -->
## Goal

Stop tracking `.aidevops.json` while preserving its local bytes.

## Files Scope

- `.aidevops.json`
- `.gitignore`

## Implementation

In a fresh linked worktree, add `.aidevops.json` to `.gitignore`, run `git rm --cached -- .aidevops.json`, and commit the index-only migration. Never delete the local file or edit a canonical checkout.

## Verification

- Confirm `.aidevops.json` remains byte-identical in the worktree.
- Confirm `git ls-files -- .aidevops.json` is empty and `.gitignore` contains the entry.
